Attach Confidence Intervals to an amerasfit Object

add_confint.Rd

Computes confidence or credible intervals, attaches them and any available diagnostics to a fitted amerasfit object, and optionally prints the bounds. Use confint when only the interval bounds are required.

Usage

add_confint(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'amerasfit'
add_confint(object, parm="dose", level=0.95,
        type=c("proflik","percentile"), maxit.profCI=20,
        tol.profCI=1e-2, data=NULL, print=TRUE,
        digits=max(3, getOption("digits") - 3), ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model object of class amerasfit, as returned by ameras.

parm

Either "dose" to compute profile likelihood intervals for dose-related parameters only, "all" for all parameters, or a character vector of parameter names. Only used when type = "proflik".

level

Confidence level, as a single number between zero and one. Defaults to 0.95.

type

Interval type. For RC, ERC, and MCML, use "wald.orig", "wald.transformed", or "proflik". For FMA and BMA, use "percentile" or "hpd". When both groups of methods are present, supply one type for each group.

maxit.profCI

Maximum number of root-finding iterations for profile likelihood intervals. Defaults to 20.

tol.profCI

Root-finding tolerance for profile likelihood intervals. Defaults to 1e-2.

data

Original fitting data. Required for profile likelihood intervals when the model was fitted with keep.data = FALSE.

print

Whether to print the attached interval bounds. Defaults to TRUE.

digits

Number of significant digits used when printing.

...

Additional arguments, currently unused.

Value

A copy of the amerasfit object, invisibly, with a CI element added to each fitted method and CI.computed set to TRUE. Method-specific timing is updated to include interval computation. The input object is not modified.

Each CI element contains lower and upper. Profile likelihood results additionally contain boundary p-values and iteration counts in pval.lower, pval.upper, iter.lower, and iter.upper.

Details

The requested intervals are always computed. Any intervals already attached to object are replaced in the returned object; the input object is left unchanged. This function is useful when the fitted object will be kept for reporting or further inspection: summary() and summary_table() include the attached bounds, profile-likelihood diagnostics are stored when available, and confidence-interval computation time is recorded in the method-specific timing information. Use confint when only standalone interval bounds are needed. Attaching intervals is particularly useful for computationally expensive profile likelihood intervals because subsequent summaries use the attached bounds and diagnostics without repeating the profile calculation. Computation and failure handling are otherwise identical.

For RC, ERC, and MCML, Wald intervals on the original parameter scale use the delta-method variance-covariance matrix. Wald intervals on the transformed scale are computed in the optimization parametrization and then back-transformed. More specifically, when \(\boldsymbol\theta = h(\boldsymbol\eta)\), transformed-scale intervals apply \(h\) to the endpoints on the \(\boldsymbol\eta\) scale, whereas original-scale intervals use the covariance matrix obtained from \(J H^{-1} J^T\), where \(J\) is the transformation Jacobian and \(H\) is the optimization Hessian. Transformed-scale intervals can therefore be asymmetric on the reported parameter scale.

For FMA and BMA, percentile intervals use equal-tailed sample quantiles and HPD intervals use HPDinterval.

See also

confint for returning interval bounds, ameras for model fitting, and summary for summaries containing attached intervals.

Examples

fit <- ameras(
  Y.binomial ~ dose(V1:V3, model = "ERR"),
  data = ameras_simulated,
  family = "binomial",
  methods = "RC"
)
#> Fitting RC

fit_with_ci <- add_confint(fit, type = "wald.orig", print = FALSE)
summary(fit_with_ci)
#> Call:
#> ameras(formula = Y.binomial ~ dose(V1:V3, model = "ERR"), data = ameras_simulated, 
#>     family = "binomial", methods = "RC")
#> 
#> Rows: 3000
#> 
#> Total CPU runtime: 0.1 seconds
#> 
#> CPU runtime in seconds by method:
#> 
#>  Method   Fit    CI Total
#>      RC 0.057 0.001 0.058
#> 
#> Summary of coefficients by method:
#> 
#>  Method        Term Estimate     SE CI.lower CI.upper
#>      RC (Intercept)  -0.8851 0.0738  -1.0297  -0.7404
#>      RC        dose   0.8044 0.1380   0.5339   1.0748
#> 

## Profile likelihood intervals are slower

fit_with_profile_ci <- add_confint(
  fit,
  type = "proflik",
  parm = "dose",
  print = FALSE
)
#> Obtaining profile likelihood CI for dose
summary(fit_with_profile_ci)
#> Call:
#> ameras(formula = Y.binomial ~ dose(V1:V3, model = "ERR"), data = ameras_simulated, 
#>     family = "binomial", methods = "RC")
#> 
#> Rows: 3000
#> 
#> Total CPU runtime: 0.1 seconds
#> 
#> CPU runtime in seconds by method:
#> 
#>  Method   Fit   CI Total
#>      RC 0.057 0.07 0.127
#> 
#> Summary of coefficients by method:
#> 
#>  Method        Term Estimate     SE CI.lower CI.upper
#>      RC (Intercept)  -0.8851 0.0738       NA       NA
#>      RC        dose   0.8044 0.1380   0.5664    1.115
#>
